# lnurlcash-core (Rust)

LNURLcash (LUD-25) bearer notes: the money-critical logic, with UniFFI bindings
for Kotlin and Swift. MIT.

cargo add lnurlcash-core

## Layout

protocol   pure: builds Requests, parses responses. No I/O. Always available.
client     optional feature "client": a thin reqwest loop over protocol.
ffi        optional feature "ffi": UniFFI export of the PURE half only.

The Request/parse split is the point: a caller with its own HTTP stack uses
protocol directly, and nothing async crosses the FFI boundary.

## Core API

protocol::note_info_request(url) -> Request { url, new_secrets, outputs }
protocol::parse_note_info(&Value, queried_url, Policy) -> WithdrawRequestInfo
protocol::rotate_request(callback, k1, new_secret) -> Request
protocol::split_request(callback, k1s, amount_msat, new_secret, change_secret) -> Request
protocol::merge_request(callback, k1s, new_secret) -> Request
protocol::melt_request(callback, k1, bolt11) -> Request
protocol::parse_mutation(&Value, MutationKind, &request.outputs, Policy)
  -> MutationResponse. outputs = what the rotate/split/merge named, recorded
  on the Request: [output], or [output, change] for a split. A cp1 output is
  owed its cs1 in c (c2 for a split's change; legacy sig/sig2 still read) ALWAYS, whatever the
  policy; without it the mutation is Unverifiable. A bearer output named by
  its hash is certified by a mint with a signer; the tolerant default admits
  None from one without. A missing output reads as a hash. Signatures come
  back as sent, unverified. MutationKind::{Melt,Rotate,Split,Merge} - a melt
  mints nothing and owes none.
protocol::Policy { require_signatures, require_mint_pubkey }  defaults false
  and true. require_signatures demands a cs1 for a bearer output too.
  require_mint_pubkey refuses a withdrawRequest with no valid mintPubkey.
  Build with ..Policy::default().
protocol::parse_note_info also returns `signature`: the c LUD-25 has the
  informational GET return for the queried note, as sent. Same on
  NoteInfoByHash.
protocol::pay_request_request / invoice_request / verify_request + parse_*

generate_note_secret() -> String    a fresh bearer preimage, 32 bytes hex
hash_k1(k1) -> Result<String>       a bearer note's h = sha256(preimage): its
  cp1 short form, what goes out as p1/p2. NOT the note's id (that is hex(Q)).

## Every note is a taproot output key Q (spend::, luds 6e865b1)

cp1<Q> names a note; a mint stores, burns and certifies it by hex(Q). A
spend (what goes where a k1 goes) opens it:
  64 hex         a bearer note's preimage = short form of its cw1
  ck1<Q||sig>    key path, BIP-340 over the key-path sighash for one domain
  cw1<...>       script path: leaf, control block, witness
A bearer note = leaf OP_SHA256 <h> OP_EQUAL (a8 20 <h> 87), version 0xc0,
under the NUMS key 50929b74...3ac0. 64 hex where a cp1 goes (comment, p1,
p2, ?p=) is h.
Every signature signs tagged_hash("TapSighash", 0x00 || SigMsg) for input 0
of one fixed tx: nVersion 2, prevout (tagged_hash("LNURLcash/mint", domain),
0), one output of value 0 with an empty script, spent output (OP_1 <Q>, 0).
domain = the mint's lowercase hostname, no scheme, NO PORT.
spend_domain_of(url_or_host) -> Option<String>
spend_prevout / spend_sig_msg / key_path_sighash(Q, domain) /
  script_path_sighash(Q, domain, leaf, locktime, sequence)   SIGHASH_DEFAULT
tagged_hash / tapleaf_hash / tapbranch_hash / taproot_tweak(P, root) ->
  TaprootTweak { output_key, parity } / taproot_tweak_secret_key /
  output_key_of(script, control_block) (fold, tweak, parity check) /
  is_x_only_point
bearer_leaf(h) / bearer_note(h) -> BearerNote { output_key, control_block,
  leaf } / bearer_cw1(preimage) -> Cw1
decode_note(cp1 or h) -> Option<Q>
decode_spend(k1) -> Option<Spend::{KeyPath, LegacyKeyPath, ScriptPath}>
check_spend(k1, domain) -> Option<SpendCheck { output_key, verdict }>
  SpendVerdict::{Opens, OpensLegacy, Unevaluated, Fails(reason)}. Only the
  bearer hashlock is evaluated; other scripts are Unevaluated. Time claims
  are the mint's clock.
check_leaf(version, script) / check_time_claim(locktime, sequence, now,
  locked_at): the mint's rules (leaf 0xc0, no OP_SUCCESSx outside pushes;
  locktime a past Unix time; relative locks time-typed and elapsed)

## Offline verification

check_note(k1, domain, amount_msat, sig, mint_pubkey) -> Option<NoteCheck {
  output_key, spend: SpendVerdict, certificate: CertifiedOver }>
  None = no spend, or the certificate does not verify. is_verified() = the
  spend opens Q at domain (current or legacy) AND the certificate verifies.
verify_note_signature(k1, domain, amount_msat, sig, mint_pubkey) -> bool
  = check_note(..).is_verified(). DOMAIN IS REQUIRED: Q and the cs1 are both
  public, so ck1<Q||junk> beside a real cs1 would otherwise pass.
check_note_url(note_url, mint_pubkey)   the same, read off
  ...?k1=<spend>&c=<cs1> (legacy &sig= still read) (domain from the URL, amount from cs1 or amount=)
check_note_certificate(cp1 or bearer h, amount, sig, mint_pubkey) ->
  Option<CertifiedOver::{OutputKey, LegacyHash}>   LegacyHash = a
  pre-taproot certificate over h
verify_note_signature_hash(id, ..) -> bool   raw: over exactly this 64-hex id
cs1 message: "LNURLcash:" || domain || ":" || amount_msat || ":" || hex(Q),
  Lightning signmessage digest, r||s||recid, recid 0..3. An amount-bearing
  cs1 must state the amount it signs in its HRP. Read only, reported as
  legacy: the message without the domain (CertifiedOver::LegacyOutputKey,
  either recid end), and over a bearer h (CertifiedOver::LegacyHash).

cash::derive_cash_root(seed) -> CashNode        BIP-32 m/139'
cash::derive_service_root(root, domain) -> S    LUD-26: m/139'/d1/d2/d3/d4,
  d1..d4 = HMAC-SHA256(privkey at m/139'/0, domain)[0..16] as 4 RAW
  big-endian uint32, domain = lowercase hostname, NO port (any URL or host
  is reduced to it). RAW: BIP-32 reads >= 2^31 as hardened, so ~half the
  levels are, decided by the domain. NEVER mask the top bit, NEVER harden
  all four - either derives a different tree and restores nothing, silently.
  Bearer notes are NOT derived from the seed (their preimage is plain
  randomness). Bearer material for every note key at that mint.
cash::derive_cash_domain_node(root, host)       the same walk over the host
  AS STORED, port included: the superseded schemes' node
cash::derive_cash_child_pub(P33, chain_code, i) BIP-32 CKDpub, non-hardened only
cash::cash_domain_indices(root, host) -> [u32; 4]   the raw d1..d4
cash::cash_node_to_hex / from_hex     privateKey || chainCode, 64 bytes
cash::derive_cash_child(node, raw_u32)          BIP-32 CKDpriv, for checking
  this crate against BIP-32's own vectors
cash::derive_cash_master(seed) -> CashNode      the BIP-32 master, for walking
  a path this crate does not name
secrets::derive_note_root / derive_note_secret  LEGACY pre-spec HMAC scheme.
  Do not mint under it; still scanned so old notes stay findable.
note::build_note_info_url_by_hash(withdraw_link, cp1 or h) -> Option<String>
  the ?p= informational GET, so a restore walk keeps spends off the wire.
  A rejection proves nothing: unknown and BURNED are one answer.
  The persisted per-host counter is the real backup, not the scan.

Key-path notes and the bech32m strings (recoverable::)
encode_cp1/decode_cp1/is_cp1   Q, 32-byte x-only, "cp". decode REFUSES a Q
  that is not a curve point
encode_ck1/decode_ck1/is_ck1   key-path spend, 96-byte Q||sig, "ck"
  decode/is also accept the legacy 65-byte recoverable-ECDSA shape so an old
  note can be rotated; DecodedCk1 identifies Current versus Legacy
encode_cw1/decode_cw1/is_cw1   script-path spend, Cw1 { locktime, sequence,
  script, control_block, witness }, "cw": u32 locktime || u32 sequence ||
  (u16 len || item)* over script, control block, witness bottom-first, all
  big-endian. decode refuses leftovers, a missing script or control block,
  and a control block committing to no key. Cw1::output_key()
encode_cs1_with_amount/decode_cs1_with_amount   mint certificate, "cs" +
  BOLT-11 amount; encode_cs1/decode_cs1 the legacy fixed "cs"
encode_cx1/decode_cx1/is_cx1   a share's xpub, Cx1 { chain_code, pubkey
  (33, compressed) }, "cx", 65 bytes, 113 chars; decode refuses a pubkey that
  is not a compressed point and the old 64-byte shape. Decoders return None,
  never panic. No 90-char limit; all-uppercase accepted; mixed case, a bech32
  (not bech32m) checksum, the wrong hrp or length and non-zero padding
  refused (BIP-350)
LUD-26 tree below S, plain BIP-32: wallet S/a'/0/i, change S/a'/1/i, share
  S/a'/2/n' (its cx1), share notes S/a'/2/n'/i (only the SERVICE picks i).
  Accounts and shares hardened; i < 2^31. Q = x(sk·G), no BIP-86 tweak
derive_note_key(S, NotePath::{Wallet{account,index}, Change{..},
  Share{account,share,index}}) -> NoteKey { secret_key, pubkey (33), output_key Q }
derive_share_node(S, account, share) -> CashNode; cash_node_to_cx1(node) -> Cx1
derive_note_pubkey(&Cx1, i) -> Q    CKDpub, what a SERVICE credits next
LEGACY, sweep only (before luds a6c4652): legacy_branch_node(root, host),
  legacy_cx1_of(node) -> LegacyCx1 (64-byte x(P)||chaincode),
  encode_/decode_legacy_cx1, legacy_derive_note_pubkey(&LegacyCx1, purpose,
  i), legacy_derive_note_secret_key(node, purpose, i); purpose None = before
  purposes, else LEGACY_PURPOSE_WALLET 0 / _CHANGE 1 / _LIGHTNING_ADDRESS 2
sign_note_ownership(sk, domain) -> [u8; 96]   Q || BIP-340 over
  key_path_sighash(Q, domain), zero aux_rand: one ck1 per key per mint,
  reproduced by seed recovery. domain = note URL, mint URL or bare host
recover_note_ownership_pubkey(payload, domain) -> Option<NoteOwner {
  pubkey_x_only, legacy }>   domain-bound sighash first; legacy: true for
  Schnorr over sha256("LNURLcash") or the raw bytes, or the 65-byte ECDSA
note_id_of(k1) -> Option<hex(Q)>   any spend. NOT sha256(k1) any more. Names
  the note; does not verify the spend (use check_spend)
note_lookup_of(k1) -> Option<String>   a bearer note's h, or cp1<Q>
Wire: any spend goes wherever a k1 does. Every output goes as p1/p2 (a cp1
  or a bearer h); *_request_with_hash REFUSE one naming no note before
  sending. mint_invoice_request_with_hash: the comment (a hash also sends h).
  Lookups go as ?p=. parse_note_info compares an echoed k1 by the note it
  names, and refuses another spend of it that fails at the queried domain.
derive_nostr_cash_seed(sk) / derive_nostr_service_root(sk, domain)   NOT
  LUD-26: the tree from a Nostr identity key, via
  HMAC-SHA256(key = sk, msg = "LNURLcash/nostr-seed"), then S from that seed
resolve_note_input / resolve_mint_input / resolve_lnurl_input
parse_mint_fee / apply_mint_fee / gross_up_for_mint_fee   "Mint fees: <base>,
  <ppm>[,<address fee>]" anywhere in text/plain, values end at whitespace;
  MintFee::address_fee_msat is LUD-26's third value (None: refuse to pay)
internal_transfer_request(pay_request, note_domain, k1, amount_msat) /
  parse_internal_transfer   LUD-26: a whole note to a Lightning Address's
  callback at the note's own mint; refused unless withdrawLink is on it
build_note_url / with_new_k1 / without_k1
address_proof_message(action, domain, username, cx1) /
  address_proof_digest(action, domain, username, cx1)
sign_address_proof(share_sk, action, domain, username, cx1) /
  verify_address_proof(signer_cx1, sig, action, domain, username, cx1)
  messages: LNURLcash:register:<domain>:<username>:<cx1>,
  LNURLcash:update:<domain>:<username>:<new cx1> (by the key on file),
  LNURLcash:unregister:<domain>:<username> (cx1 None); username lowercased,
  domain = the SERVICE's hostname; raw 64-byte BIP-340 over sha256(message)
  by the share's own key, verified against x(P) of the signer's cx1
decode_bolt11_amount_msat / is_bolt11_invoice / same_invoice

client::Client::{fetch_note_info, fetch_note_info_by_hash, rotate_note,
split_note, merge_notes, melt_note, settle_note, probe_burned_note,
fetch_pay_request, request_invoice, fetch_invoice_verification,
fetch_mint_address}

## Errors

Error::RequestRefused   nothing sent, note untouched
Error::ServiceRejected  processed and refused (definitive)
Error::NotePending      a melt is in flight on this k1 - retry, NOT spent
Error::NoteSpent { reason, new_secrets }    authoritative at the info GET.
  From a MUTATION at a service that will not replay a retry, it is also what
  an ALREADY-APPLIED mutation looks like - read new_secrets before believing
Error::NoteUnknown { reason, new_secrets }  service does not recognise it
Error::Ambiguous { message, new_secrets }   outcome UNKNOWN
Error::Unverifiable { message, new_secrets }  the mutation LANDED and a cp1
  output came back with no cs1 (or a bearer output uncertified under
  require_signatures). The note is REAL - persist new_secrets (empty from a
  *_with_hash call: the caller holds that key), then report the mint
Error::Protocol         a non-mutating response did not match the spec,
  which includes a withdrawRequest publishing no mintPubkey (unless
  require_mint_pubkey is off)
err.is_output_in_use()  ServiceRejected("already in use"): a p1/p2 names a
  note already outstanding or burned. Nothing burned; retry at the next index

err.is_ambiguous() and err.is_definitive() are the two questions worth asking.
err.new_secrets() carries the secrets out of any error that could describe a
mutation the service applied - ambiguous, unverifiable, spent or unknown.
PERSIST them before anything else, then probe_burned_note.

client::ClientConfig { policy, mutation_retries, .. }
  mutation_retries defaults to 1. LUD-25 requires a service to answer a
  byte-identical retried rotate/split/merge with the original success, so a
  lost answer is re-asked rather than given up on. NEVER a melt: it carries
  pr, is paid asynchronously and has no replay guarantee. The request is
  re-sent byte for byte - the replay is matched on the notes the k1s open,
  p1, p2 and amount, so a fresh secret would make it a different mutation.

## Rules

1. max_withdrawable is the ONLY authoritative value. A note URL's `amount` is a claim.
2. The WALLET generates replacement notes; disclose only sha256(preimage)
   or a cp1. Never accept a service-supplied k1.
3. Ambiguous means MAYBE. Save new_secrets, then probe.
4. A melt's OK means IN FLIGHT.
5. Rotate immediately after claiming a minted note.
6. Never log note URLs - the secret is in the query string.
7. Amounts are integer milli-satoshis, u64, everywhere.

## Porting hazards (both in the vectors)

- floor(gross*ppm/1e6) overflows u64 at realistic amounts. Compute split:
  (g/1e6)*ppm + ((g%1e6)*ppm)/1e6
- gross-up must be binary search; estimate-then-walk is unbounded near 100% fee.

## Bindings

cargo run --features bindgen --bin uniffi-bindgen -- generate \
  --library target/release/liblnurlcash_core.dylib --language kotlin --out-dir bindings

FfiRequest { url, new_secrets, outputs }
FfiPolicy { require_signatures = false, require_mint_pubkey = true }
parse_note_info(body, queried_url, FfiPolicy) -> FfiWithdrawInfo (+ signature)
parse_note_info_by_hash(body, FfiPolicy) -> FfiNoteInfoByHash
parse_mutation(body, new_secrets, kind, outputs, FfiPolicy) -> FfiMutation
  pass request.newSecrets AND request.outputs back: without outputs a cp1
  output is read as a hash and its missing certificate goes unnoticed
sign_note_ownership(sk_hex, domain)   verify_note_signature(k1, domain, ..)
check_note / check_note_url -> FfiNoteCheck { output_key, spend:
  FfiSpendVerdict, certificate: FfiCertifiedOver, verified }
check_spend(k1, domain) -> FfiSpendCheck; recover_note_ownership_pubkey(hex,
  domain) -> FfiNoteOwner { pubkey_x_only, legacy }
sign_address_proof(sk0_hex, action, domain, username)
FfiCw1 + encode_cw1/decode_cw1/is_cw1/bearer_cw1; spend_domain_of,
  key_path_sighash, script_path_sighash, tapleaf_hash, tapbranch_hash,
  taproot_tweak, taproot_tweak_secret_key, output_key_of, bearer_note,
  decode_note, is_x_only_point, check_leaf, check_time_claim
